title: Consensus recommendations on training and competing in the heat
authors: Racinais S, Alonso JM, Coutts AJ, Flouris AD, Girard O, Gonzalez-Alonso J, et al.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Expert consensus (17 authors per Crossref) for athletes training and competing in hot conditions
findings: Heat acclimatization is the most important intervention to reduce physiological strain and optimize performance in the heat.
Heat acclimatization should comprise repeated exercise-heat exposures over 1-2 weeks.
Athletes should start competition and training euhydrated and minimize dehydration during exercise.
Cooling strategies (e.g. cooling vest) can be used before training or competing to facilitate heat loss or raise heat storage capacity.
Organizers should schedule events to minimize health risk, especially for mass participation events and during the first hot days of the year.
limitations: Consensus statement with no pooled effect sizes in the abstract; elite and team-sport oriented; cooling and hydration advice not specific to ultra distances.
implications: If forecast race WBGT is in a moderate-or-higher heat band, schedule 7-14 days of heat exposure before the race and flag plans lacking such a window.
Flag the first hot days of a season as higher risk: reduce intensity targets and show a warning.
Add a pre-session reminder to start euhydrated; no numeric hydration target is justified by this abstract.

verification.notes: Crossref (SJMSS, online 2015-05, print 2015-06; 17 authors) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched. Co-published copies (BJSM, Sports Med) omitted as duplicates. Graded A per the consensus rule, but it gives no effect sizes, so rules from it carry only moderate confidence.
